what_its_for: Mupirocin is an antibiotic ointment or cream used to treat skin infections caused by bacteria. It is most commonly used to treat impetigo (a skin infection that causes sores or blisters), as well as minor infected cuts, scrapes, and wounds. Your doctor may also prescribe it to apply inside your nose to get rid of a germ called MRSA (methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus).
how_to_take: Wash your hands before and after using this medicine. Clean and dry the affected skin area gently before applying. Use a clean cotton swab or your fingertip to apply a small amount of ointment or cream to the infected area. Cover the area with a bandage or gauze if your doctor recommends it. Do not get this medicine in your eyes, nose, or mouth unless your doctor has specifically told you to use it in your nose. If you accidentally get it in your eyes, rinse well with water right away. Only use this medicine on your skin (or inside your nostrils if prescribed for that purpose). Do not swallow it.
dosing: For skin infections: Apply a small amount to the affected area 3 times a day (morning, afternoon, and evening) for 5 to 10 days, or as directed by your doctor. For nasal use (to eliminate MRSA): Apply a small amount inside each nostril 2 times a day (morning and evening) for 5 days. Your doctor will tell you exactly how long to use this medicine. Always follow your doctor's instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store mupirocin at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the tube tightly closed when not in use. Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not freeze. Keep this medicine out of reach of children. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the tube.
what_to_avoid: Do not use mupirocin on large areas of the body unless your doctor tells you to. Avoid getting this medicine in your eyes — if this happens, rinse with water right away. Do not use other skin products, lotions, or cosmetics on the treated area unless your doctor approves. Avoid sharing this medicine with others, even if they have similar symptoms. Do not use mupirocin longer than prescribed, as overuse can cause the bacteria to become resistant, meaning the medicine may stop working.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if: your skin infection does not start to improve within 3 to 5 days of treatment; the infected area gets worse, more red, more swollen, or more painful; you develop a rash, hives, severe itching, or swelling of your face, lips, or throat (this could be a sign of a serious allergic reaction — call 911 or go to the emergency room immediately); you develop severe diarrhea or stomach cramps, which could signal a different type of infection; or you have any other new or concerning symptoms while using this medicine.
when_it_works: Most people start to see improvement in their skin infection within 3 to 5 days of starting mupirocin. It is very important to keep using the medicine for the full number of days your doctor prescribed, even if the skin looks better sooner. Stopping too early can allow the infection to come back.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Mupirocin is considered generally safe during pregnancy and breastfeeding when used as directed, but always tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding before using this medicine. Children: Mupirocin can be used in children, including infants, but always follow your doctor's specific instructions for dosing and application in young children. Kidney or liver problems: Since mupirocin is applied to the skin and very little is absorbed into the body, it is generally safe for people with kidney or liver problems. However, always inform your doctor about all of your medical conditions before starting any new medicine. Elderly patients: Older adults can use mupirocin safely, but should follow the same precautions as other patients.
